pages.text: The Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah and stayed in its upper part, in a quarter whose people were called Banu Amr ibn Awf, and he stayed among them for fourteen nights.
Then he sent for Banu an-Najjar and they came. He ﷺ was on his mount with Abu Bakr riding behind him, and Banu an-Najjar around him, until he stopped in the courtyard of the house of Abu Ayyub.

He ﷺ loved to pray wherever the time of prayer reached him. Then he ordered the mosque to be built, and said to Banu an-Najjar: “O Banu an-Najjar, name me a price for this walled garden of yours.” (Sahih al-Bukhari 428) — that is: sell me this garden of yours.
They said: “No, by Allah! We seek its price only from Allah.” (Sahih al-Bukhari 428). In the garden there were ruins and palm trees: the ruins were levelled, and the palm trees were cut down.

They set the palm trunks in a row as the qiblah of the mosque, made the two sides of its door of stone, and began carrying the rocks, chanting verses as they worked, and the Prophet ﷺ was with them, saying: “O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun.” (Sahih al-Bukhari 428)
In this story, Banu an-Najjar gave their garden seeking its price only from Allah, and the Prophet ﷺ was with his companions as they carried the rocks, praying for the Ansar and the Muhajirun.
